DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http Ilwww. dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 76 s. 2022 AUG 04 2022 LITO NARCISO E. CREUS Former Mayor Municipality of Malabuyoc, Cebu Dear Mr. Creus: This has reference to your letter dated June 8, 2022, with attachments requesting the Department's guidance as to how you shall proceed with the turn-over of the municipal matters to the new set of municipal officials on June 30, 2022 since the proclaimed Mayor (Ms. Erlinda Piedad) has been recently dismissed from government service. In sum, your request involves an incoming Local Chief Executive who was dismissed from government service by virtue of a decision from the Office of the Ombudsman with an accessory penalty of cancellation of eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits and perpetual disqualification from government service prior to the concluded national and !ocal elections. It may be recalled that on July 01, 2019, the Department issued a Memorandum re ON THE MATTER OF DISMISSED AND SUSPENDED LOCAL ELECTIVE OFFICIALS WHO RAN, WON, AND PROCLAIMED AS WINNERS LAST 13 MAY 2019 ELECTIONS visa-vis the 13 May 2019 Elections, pertinent portion of which reads: "In view of the recently concluded National and Local Elections held last 13 May 2019, the Department has been confronted with issues on whether local elective officials who were dismissed from service or placed under suspension shall continuously serve the imposed penalty after the said official ran, won and proclaimed as a winner. There local elective officials shall continuously serve the imposed penalty (dismissal, preventive suspension or suspension as a penalty) following verbal communication with Honorable Ombudsman Samuel R. Martires that those who have started serving their penalty shall continue to serve the same despite their re-election to the same or different position. Honorable Martires will be issuing a formal communication directing the same." Further, under the Ombudsman Rules, its decisions in administrative cases shall be executed as a matter of course and that an appeal shall not stop the decision from "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

being executory. Therefore, when the Department implemented the order of dismissal against Piedad, he was effectively removed from office. In the case of Tallado vs. COMELEC, et al. the Supreme Court explained, to wit: "Moreover, it should be pointed out that the decisions directing the dismissal of the petitioner included no indication of the petitioner being thereby placed under any type of suspension. In fact, the decisions did not state any conditions whatsoever. As such, he was dismissed for all intents and purposes of the law in the periods that he was dismissed from office even if he had appealed. In that status, he ceased to hold the title to the office in the fullest sense." Considering that the OMB decision dismissing Piedad was served against him on April 12, 2022, his victory of garnering the highest votes as Mayor of Malabuyoc will not entitle him to assume the duties and responsibilities of the Mayor. Consequently, there will be a permanent vacancy in the Office of the Mayor. Section 44 of the Local Government Code of 1991 enumerates instances when permanent vacancy arises in the Offices of the Governor, Vice-Governor, Mayor and Vice-Mayor, viz: Section 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices of the Governor, Vice- Governor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor. - If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the governor or mayor, the vice-governor or vice-mayor concerned shall become the governor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs in the offices of the governor, vice-governor, mayor, or vice- mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the governor, vice-governor, mayor or vice-mayor, as the case may be. Subsequent vacancies in the said office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined herein. xxx For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. (emphasis ours) Hence, the elected Vice-Mayor will assume as Mayor while the highest Sangguniang Bayan Member, upon request of the concerned SB Member and designationl by the Secretary of DILG and the turn-over of municipal matters should be directed them. 1 Pursuant to Administrative Order No. 15 dated December 13, 2018 issued by the President authorizing the DILG Secretary or its Officer-in-Charge to fill temporary vacancies in certain local government offices to prevent hiatus in and paralysis of local government operations and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-21.

We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: I AN ry for Local Government Undersecr OUSLG/MLl/LLLS-LRALLD/clp/OD/518 Copy furnished: DIRECTOR LEOCADIO T.
